Archive item 1: Annual General Meeting Minutes – 14 March 2023
Source format: Meeting Minutes

Amelia Hartley presented the annual report for the year ending 31 December 2022. She highlighted the successful refurbishment of the junior changing rooms, which was completed in August 2022 within the budget approved at the 2022 AGM. She noted that the club had seen a 12% increase in junior membership across football and cricket sections. She thanked the volunteer grounds team for their work during the wet winter months and acknowledged the outgoing committee members for their service.

She also mentioned that the club had received a grant of £2,500 from the Parish Council toward the new floodlighting project, and that a further application for funding had been submitted to the Sports England Small Grants scheme. The Chairperson confirmed that the club’s safeguarding policy had been reviewed and updated in line with current guidance, and that all coaching staff had completed their DBS checks.

**3. Treasurer’s Report**

James Okafor presented the audited accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022. Copies of the income and expenditure statement and the balance sheet were distributed to members present. Key points:

- Total income for 2022: £74,380 (2021: £61,205)
- Total expenditure: £68,915 (2021: £57,480)
- Net surplus for the year: £5,465
- Cash at bank as at 31 December 2022: £18,230, of which £6,000 is held in the sinking fund for the clubhouse roof replacement.

The Treasurer noted that the increase in income was primarily due to the resumption of full league fixtures and the return of the summer social programme. Expenditure included the junior changing room works (£9,800), new cricket nets (£4,200), and increased utility costs. He proposed that the annual subscription rates for 2023–24 be set at £45 for adults and £25 for juniors, with a family cap of £100. This was seconded by Fiona Grant and carried by a majority vote.

The audited accounts were formally adopted by the meeting, proposed by Alan Whitfield and seconded by Carol Bates.

**4. Election of Officers for 2023–24**

The Secretary read the list of nominations received for the committee positions. Where more than one nomination was received, a ballot was held. The following officers were elected for the year 2023–24:

The AGM minutes record that Amelia Hartley was elected as chairperson on 2023-03-14. Record status: historical.

- **Chairperson:** Amelia Hartley (proposed by Margaret Ellison, seconded by David Chen; no other nominations received)
- **Vice-Chairperson:** Tom Ashworth (proposed by Susan Reed, seconded by Ben Wright)
- **Secretary:** Priya Nair (proposed by Richard Holmes, seconded by Jill Harper)
- **Treasurer:** James Okafor (proposed by Alan Whitfield, seconded by Carol Bates)
- **Membership Secretary:** Helen Park (proposed by Mohammed Farouk, seconded by Andrew Lowe)
- **Social Secretary:** Fiona Grant (proposed by Peter Madden, seconded by Emma Stone)
- **Welfare Officer:** Margaret Ellison (proposed by Amelia Hartley, seconded by Linda Boyd)

The meeting recorded that Amelia Hartley was elected as chairperson on 14 March 2023, and she resumed the chair for the remainder of the meeting.

**5. Election of Committee Members**

Seven ordinary committee members were elected to serve alongside the officers. The following were elected by ballot: David Chen, Susan Reed, Alan Whitfield, Carol Bates, Richard Holmes, Ben Wright, and George Mercer. The meeting thanked the outgoing ordinary members, Sandra Okafor, Chris Duffy, and Tony Wells, for their contributions.

**6. Appointment of Auditor**

It was resolved that the firm of Whitfield & Co. be re-appointed as the club’s independent examiner for the financial year ending 31 December 2023, proposed by James Okafor and seconded by Amelia Hartley.

**7. Reports from Sections**

**7.1 Football Section** – Tom Ashworth reported that the senior men’s first team finished fourth in the County League Division Two, and the women’s team finished third in the Regional League. The youth section had fielded teams at U11, U13, and U15 levels. A new girls’ U13 team would be formed for the coming season, subject to sufficient volunteer coaches. The section would hold a pre-season meeting in June.
James Okafor presented the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022. Copies of the income and expenditure account and the balance sheet had been circulated with the notice of the meeting. He drew members’ attention to the following points:

- Total income for the year was £84,210, compared with £78,640 in 2021.
- Total expenditure was £79,880, leaving a surplus of £4,330.
- The main increases in expenditure were in ground maintenance (£1,850) and electricity (£1,120).
- Bar takings had recovered to pre-pandemic levels.
- The club’s reserves stood at £23,410, of which £8,000 was earmarked for the proposed cricket pitch works.

James noted that the accounts had been examined by Whitfield & Co. and that the independent examiner had raised no matters of concern.

A member asked about the level of the club’s reserves and whether it was appropriate to hold such a sum. James explained that the committee had agreed a target of keeping reserves at roughly three months’ running costs, and that the current figure was slightly above this. It was expected that the cricket pitch works would draw down a significant part of the surplus in the coming year.

**Resolved:** That the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022, as circulated, be adopted. Proposed by Alan Whitfield, seconded by Susan Reed. Carried unanimously.

**9. Budget for 2023 and Membership Fees**

The Treasurer presented a draft budget for the year ending 31 December 2023, which showed a projected surplus of £1,900. The main assumptions were:

- A 3% increase in bar prices from 1 April.
- A 5% increase in electricity costs.
- No increase in the club’s grant to the cricket pitch fund in 2023.

The meeting discussed the level of membership fees for 2023–24. After some debate, it was proposed that the annual subscription be increased from £45 to £50 for a full adult member, and from £25 to £28 for a junior member. The family rate would remain at £110.

An amendment was proposed that the junior rate should not be increased, on the grounds that the club should encourage younger members. The amendment was put to the vote and was lost by 12 votes to 31.

The original motion was then put to the meeting.

The AGM minutes record that James Whitfield was elected as treasurer on 2023-03-14. Record status: historical.

**Resolved:** That, with effect from 1 June 2023, the annual subscription be increased to £50 for a full adult member and £28 for a junior member, and that the family rate remain at £110. Proposed by the Committee, seconded by Margaret Ellison. Carried by 38 votes to 5.

**10. Election of Officers**

The Secretary reported that nominations had closed at 7.00 pm on the day of the meeting. The following officers were elected for the year 2023–24:

- **Chairperson:** Amelia Hartley (proposed by Margaret Ellison, seconded by David Chen; no other nominations received)
- **Vice-Chairperson:** Tom Ashworth (proposed by Susan Reed, seconded by Ben Wright)
- **Secretary:** Priya Nair (proposed by Richard Holmes, seconded by Jill Harper)
- **Treasurer:** James Okafor (proposed by Alan Whitfield, seconded by Carol Bates)
- **Membership Secretary:** Helen Park (proposed by Mohammed Farouk, seconded by Andrew Lowe)
- **Social Secretary:** Fiona Grant (proposed by Peter Madden, seconded by Emma Stone)
- **Welfare Officer:** Margaret Ellison (proposed by Amelia Hartley, seconded by Linda Boyd)

The meeting recorded that Amelia Hartley was elected as chairperson on 14 March 2023, and she resumed the chair for the remainder of the meeting.

**11. Election of Committee Members**

Seven ordinary committee members were elected to serve alongside the officers. The following were elected by ballot: David Chen, Susan Reed, Alan Whitfield, Carol Bates, Richard Holmes, Ben Wright, and George Mercer. The meeting thanked the outgoing ordinary members, Sandra Okafor, Chris Duffy, and Tony Wells, for their contributions.

**12. Appointment of Auditor**

It was resolved that the firm of Whitfield & Co. be re-appointed as the club’s independent examiner for the financial year ending 31 December 2023, proposed by James Okafor and seconded by Amelia Hartley.

**13. Reports from Sections**
**Ladies’ Section.** Susan Reed reported that the Ladies’ Section had held its AGM on 7 March. The Captain for the coming year, Linda Boyd, had been elected at that meeting, with Carol Bates as Vice-Captain. The Section had agreed to hold a charity coffee morning on 22 April in aid of the local hospice, and asked that the clubhouse booking be confirmed. The Section also raised the question of the condition of the path from the car park to the first tee, which had become muddy in places; this was referred to the House Committee for action.

**Juniors’ Section.** Ben Wright reported that the junior coaching programme would begin on Saturday 15 April, run by the club professional. There were currently 14 juniors enrolled, and the Section was keen to see this number increase. It was agreed that the Secretary would write to the local schools to advertise the programme. The Section also proposed a junior open day on 28 May, to coincide with the club’s open day, and this was welcomed by the meeting.

**House Committee.** Margaret Ellison reported that the kitchen refurbishment, approved at the last Committee meeting, had been completed on schedule. The new dishwasher had been installed, and the store room had been reorganised. A small leak had been discovered under the sink in the men’s locker room, and a plumber had been instructed to attend on 21 March. The Committee had also agreed to purchase new curtains for the lounge, and samples would be available for inspection at the next meeting.

**14. Constitutional Amendments**

The Secretary read out the proposed amendments to the club constitution, which had been circulated to members with the notice of the meeting. The following resolutions were put to the meeting:

**Resolution 1:** That Rule 7 (Committee) be amended to provide that the Committee may co-opt up to two additional members, rather than one, for the purposes of filling a vacancy or for a specific task. Proposed by the Committee, seconded by Fiona Grant. The amendment was carried by 30 votes to 12.

**Resolution 2:** That Rule 12 (Discipline) be amended to provide that a member suspended for more than three months shall have the right to appeal to a special general meeting, rather than to the Committee. Proposed by David Chen, seconded by Alan Whitfield. After discussion, the amendment was carried by 27 votes to 15.

**Resolution 3:** That Rule 15 (Alteration of Rules) be amended to require a two-thirds majority of those present and voting at a general meeting for any future alteration, rather than a simple majority. Proposed by the Committee, seconded by Helen Park. The amendment was carried by 33 votes to 9.

The Secretary noted that the amended constitution would come into effect on 1 April 2023, and that a copy would be available on the club noticeboard and from the Secretary.

**15. Any Other Business**

- The Chairperson reported that the club had received a donation of £250 from the estate of a former member, the late Mr. Harold Simmons, and that this had been placed in the general fund. The meeting recorded its thanks.
- A member asked whether the club would be entering a team in the local inter-club league this season. The Chairperson confirmed that the Committee had agreed to enter a team, and that the captain would be appointed at the next Committee meeting.
- It was noted that the car park resurfacing, approved at the last AGM, had been completed in February, and that the new markings were now in place.
- The Chairperson thanked the retiring Committee members and all volunteers for their work during the past year.

**16. Election of Priya Sharma as Secretary**

The AGM minutes record that Priya Sharma was elected as secretary on 2023-03-14. Record status: historical.

**17. Date of Next Meeting**

The next Annual General Meeting will be held on Tuesday 12 March 2024 at 7.30 pm in the clubhouse. The next Committee meeting will be held on Tuesday 4 April 2023 at 7.30 pm.

**18. Adjournment**

There being no further business, the Chairperson declared the meeting closed at 9.45 pm.

**Signatures**

Chairperson: ___________________________

Secretary: ___________________________

Date: ___________________________
**Annual General Meeting Minutes – 14 March 2023** *(continued)*

**19. Presentation of Awards**

The Chairperson presented the following trophies and awards for the 2022 season:

- **Men’s Singles Champion:** Tom Becker
- **Ladies’ Singles Champion:** Sarah Okafor
- **Men’s Doubles Champions:** David Chen and Alan Whitfield
- **Ladies’ Doubles Champions:** Helen Park and Margaret Doyle
- **Mixed Doubles Champions:** Priya Sharma and James Okafor
- **Most Improved Player:** Lucy Nguyen
- **Clubperson of the Year:** Harold Simmons (posthumous), accepted by his niece, Mrs. Eileen Porter, who attended the meeting as a guest. Mrs. Porter thanked the club on behalf of the family and noted that her uncle had been a member for over forty years.

The Chairperson proposed a vote of thanks to Mrs. Porter for attending and for the family’s continued support of the club. This was carried unanimously.

**20. Thanks to Outgoing Officers**

The meeting recorded its sincere thanks to the outgoing Secretary, Mr. Alan Whitfield, for his six years of service in that role, and to the outgoing Treasurer, Mrs. Margaret Doyle, for her careful stewardship of the club’s finances. Both had indicated that they were not seeking re-election at this meeting. The Chairperson also thanked the retiring Committee members, namely Mrs. Eileen Porter, Mr. Robert Gaines, and Ms. Anita Desai, for their contributions.

A vote of thanks to all outgoing officers and committee members was proposed by Mr. David Chen, seconded by Mrs. Sarah Okafor, and carried unanimously.

**21. General Announcements**

- The Chairperson reminded members that the clubhouse would be closed for deep cleaning from Monday 20 March to Wednesday 22 March inclusive, and that the bar would reopen on Thursday 23 March at 6.00 pm.
- The annual club dinner will be held on Saturday 22 April 2023 at the Riverside Hotel, starting at 7.00 for 7.30 pm. Tickets are £28 per person and are available from the bar or from the Secretary. Numbers are limited to 80.
- The club’s summer tournament entry forms will be available from 1 April 2023. The entry fee is £10 per event, with a maximum of three events per person. Entries close on Saturday 20 May 2023.
- The Committee has agreed to trial a new online booking system for court hire. The system will go live on 1 April 2023, and a demonstration will be held in the clubhouse on Saturday 25 March at 10.00 am. Members who do not wish to use the online system may continue to book by telephone or at the bar.
- The club’s annual subscription for the coming year remains unchanged at £120 for full members, £80 for social members, and £30 for juniors. Renewal notices will be sent out in early April, and payment is due by 1 May 2023.
- A reminder that the club is now registered with the local council’s “Safe Sport” initiative, and all members are asked to familiarise themselves with the updated safeguarding policy, a copy of which is available on the noticeboard.
- The Chairperson noted that the club had received a grant of £500 from the Borough Council towards the cost of new court floodlights, and that the remaining balance would be met from the general fund. Work is expected to commence in late April.
- It was announced that the club’s junior section would be running a free taster session on Saturday 1 April 2023, from 10.00 am to 12.00 noon, and members were encouraged to spread the word among friends and neighbours.

**22. Attendance and Apologies**

The following members were recorded as present at the meeting:

Mr. David Chen (Chairperson), Mr. Alan Whitfield (Secretary), Mrs. Margaret Doyle (Treasurer), Priya Sharma, Helen Park, Sarah Okafor, James Okafor, Tom Becker, Lucy Nguyen, Alan Whitfield, Mrs. Eileen Porter (guest), Mr. Robert Gaines, Ms. Anita Desai, and approximately 45 other members whose names are recorded in the attendance book held by the Secretary.

Apologies for absence were received from:

- Mr. George Fletcher
- Mrs. Joan Mercer
- Mr. Peter Hutton
- Ms. Claire Donovan
- Mr. Richard Ellis
- Mrs. Sylvia Grant
- Mr. Frank Underwood
- Ms. Barbara Chen (no relation to the Chairperson)

documents.title: Annual General Meeting Minutes – 14 March 2023
documents.content:
Amelia Hartley presented the annual report for the year ending 31 December 2022. She highlighted the successful refurbishment of the junior changing rooms, which was completed in August 2022 within the budget approved at the 2022 AGM. She noted that the club had seen a 12% increase in junior membership across football and cricket sections. She thanked the volunteer grounds team for their work during the wet winter months and acknowledged the outgoing committee members for their service.

She also mentioned that the club had received a grant of £2,500 from the Parish Council toward the new floodlighting project, and that a further application for funding had been submitted to the Sports England Small Grants scheme. The Chairperson confirmed that the club’s safeguarding policy had been reviewed and updated in line with current guidance, and that all coaching staff had completed their DBS checks.

**3. Treasurer’s Report**

James Okafor presented the audited accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022. Copies of the income and expenditure statement and the balance sheet were distributed to members present. Key points:

- Total income for 2022: £74,380 (2021: £61,205)
- Total expenditure: £68,915 (2021: £57,480)
- Net surplus for the year: £5,465
- Cash at bank as at 31 December 2022: £18,230, of which £6,000 is held in the sinking fund for the clubhouse roof replacement.

The Treasurer noted that the increase in income was primarily due to the resumption of full league fixtures and the return of the summer social programme. Expenditure included the junior changing room works (£9,800), new cricket nets (£4,200), and increased utility costs. He proposed that the annual subscription rates for 2023–24 be set at £45 for adults and £25 for juniors, with a family cap of £100. This was seconded by Fiona Grant and carried by a majority vote.

The audited accounts were formally adopted by the meeting, proposed by Alan Whitfield and seconded by Carol Bates.

**4. Election of Officers for 2023–24**

The Secretary read the list of nominations received for the committee positions. Where more than one nomination was received, a ballot was held. The following officers were elected for the year 2023–24:

The AGM minutes record that Amelia Hartley was elected as chairperson on 2023-03-14. Record status: historical.

- **Chairperson:** Amelia Hartley (proposed by Margaret Ellison, seconded by David Chen; no other nominations received)
- **Vice-Chairperson:** Tom Ashworth (proposed by Susan Reed, seconded by Ben Wright)
- **Secretary:** Priya Nair (proposed by Richard Holmes, seconded by Jill Harper)
- **Treasurer:** James Okafor (proposed by Alan Whitfield, seconded by Carol Bates)
- **Membership Secretary:** Helen Park (proposed by Mohammed Farouk, seconded by Andrew Lowe)
- **Social Secretary:** Fiona Grant (proposed by Peter Madden, seconded by Emma Stone)
- **Welfare Officer:** Margaret Ellison (proposed by Amelia Hartley, seconded by Linda Boyd)

The meeting recorded that Amelia Hartley was elected as chairperson on 14 March 2023, and she resumed the chair for the remainder of the meeting.

**5. Election of Committee Members**

Seven ordinary committee members were elected to serve alongside the officers. The following were elected by ballot: David Chen, Susan Reed, Alan Whitfield, Carol Bates, Richard Holmes, Ben Wright, and George Mercer. The meeting thanked the outgoing ordinary members, Sandra Okafor, Chris Duffy, and Tony Wells, for their contributions.

**6. Appointment of Auditor**

It was resolved that the firm of Whitfield & Co. be re-appointed as the club’s independent examiner for the financial year ending 31 December 2023, proposed by James Okafor and seconded by Amelia Hartley.

**7. Reports from Sections**

**7.1 Football Section** – Tom Ashworth reported that the senior men’s first team finished fourth in the County League Division Two, and the women’s team finished third in the Regional League. The youth section had fielded teams at U11, U13, and U15 levels. A new girls’ U13 team would be formed for the coming season, subject to sufficient volunteer coaches. The section would hold a pre-season meeting in June.

- The main increases in expenditure were in ground maintenance (£1,850) and electricity (£1,120).

- The club’s reserves stood at £23,410, of which £8,000 was earmarked for the proposed cricket pitch works.

James noted that the accounts had been examined by Whitfield & Co. and that the independent examiner had raised no matters of concern.

A member asked about the level of the club’s reserves and whether it was appropriate to hold such a sum. James explained that the committee had agreed a target of keeping reserves at roughly three months’ running costs, and that the current figure was slightly above this. It was expected that the cricket pitch works would draw down a significant part of the surplus in the coming year.

**Resolved:** That the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022, as circulated, be adopted. Proposed by Alan Whitfield, seconded by Susan Reed. Carried unanimously.

- A 3% increase in bar prices from 1 April.

The original motion was then put to the meeting.

documents.title: Annual General Meeting Minutes – 14 March 2023
documents.content:
**Ladies’ Section.** Susan Reed reported that the Ladies’ Section had held its AGM on 7 March. The Captain for the coming year, Linda Boyd, had been elected at that meeting, with Carol Bates as Vice-Captain. The Section had agreed to hold a charity coffee morning on 22 April in aid of the local hospice, and asked that the clubhouse booking be confirmed. The Section also raised the question of the condition of the path from the car park to the first tee, which had become muddy in places; this was referred to the House Committee for action.

**Juniors’ Section.** Ben Wright reported that the junior coaching programme would begin on Saturday 15 April, run by the club professional. There were currently 14 juniors enrolled, and the Section was keen to see this number increase. It was agreed that the Secretary would write to the local schools to advertise the programme. The Section also proposed a junior open day on 28 May, to coincide with the club’s open day, and this was welcomed by the meeting.

**House Committee.** Margaret Ellison reported that the kitchen refurbishment, approved at the last Committee meeting, had been completed on schedule. The new dishwasher had been installed, and the store room had been reorganised. A small leak had been discovered under the sink in the men’s locker room, and a plumber had been instructed to attend on 21 March. The Committee had also agreed to purchase new curtains for the lounge, and samples would be available for inspection at the next meeting.

**14. Constitutional Amendments**

The Secretary read out the proposed amendments to the club constitution, which had been circulated to members with the notice of the meeting. The following resolutions were put to the meeting:

**Resolution 1:** That Rule 7 (Committee) be amended to provide that the Committee may co-opt up to two additional members, rather than one, for the purposes of filling a vacancy or for a specific task. Proposed by the Committee, seconded by Fiona Grant. The amendment was carried by 30 votes to 12.

**Resolution 2:** That Rule 12 (Discipline) be amended to provide that a member suspended for more than three months shall have the right to appeal to a special general meeting, rather than to the Committee. Proposed by David Chen, seconded by Alan Whitfield. After discussion, the amendment was carried by 27 votes to 15.

**Resolution 3:** That Rule 15 (Alteration of Rules) be amended to require a two-thirds majority of those present and voting at a general meeting for any future alteration, rather than a simple majority. Proposed by the Committee, seconded by Helen Park. The amendment was carried by 33 votes to 9.

The Secretary noted that the amended constitution would come into effect on 1 April 2023, and that a copy would be available on the club noticeboard and from the Secretary.

The AGM minutes record that Priya Sharma was elected as secretary on 2023-03-14. Record status: historical.

The next Annual General Meeting will be held on Tuesday 12 March 2024 at 7.30 pm in the clubhouse. The next Committee meeting will be held on Tuesday 4 April 2023 at 7.30 pm.

Current paid-up membership: 214 senior, 89 junior, 23 social. This compares with 201 senior, 77 junior, 19 social at the same point last year. R. A. Cole reported that the main pitch had recovered well from the winter. However, he raised two concerns:

- The Parish Council letter (see item 1) asks the club to cut back the hedge before the end of April to maintain visibility at the junction with the access road.
- The hot water in the away team changing room is intermittent; the immersion heater appears to be faulty.

The committee minutes record that Tom Okafor was appointed as facilities manager on 2023-04-01. Record status: current.

The Chair explained that the committee had previously agreed to create a new paid role of Facilities Manager, combining oversight of the clubhouse, grounds equipment and minor repairs, in response to the growing workload on volunteers. The post had been advertised internally and externally; three applications had been received.

The Chair invited T. Okafor, who had been shortlisted, to address the committee briefly. T. Okafor outlined his experience in building maintenance and his history as a club member and occasional volunteer. He answered questions from the committee regarding availability (approximately 10 hours per week), willingness to be on call for emergencies, and his approach to prioritising tasks.

The committee then considered the appointment in closed session. It was resolved that the committee minutes record that Tom Okafor was appointed as facilities manager on 2023-04-01. The appointment is effective immediately and will be reviewed after a six-month probationary period.

**Decision 5.1:** T. Okafor appointed as Facilities Manager, with effect from 1 April 2023. Salary as per the agreed schedule (Grade 2, point 6), paid monthly. The Facilities Manager will report to the Grounds sub-committee on maintenance matters and to the Chair on health and safety matters.

S. Granger reported that the Easter Sunday quiz had been well attended. The next planned events are a curry night on 22 April and the May Day bank holiday barbecue on 1 May. She requested a small budget for prizes. The committee agreed to allocate up to £40.

K. Brooks reminded the committee that all junior coaches and volunteers must have an up-to-date DBS check on file. Three coaches are due for renewal in May; she will contact them directly. documents.title: Committee Meeting Minutes – 1 April 2023
documents.content:
The committee also discussed the membership fees for the coming season. P. Delaney reported that the current fees were £45 for a full adult member, £25 for a junior, and £15 for a social member, with a family rate of £100. He noted that the fees had not increased for three years and that the club's running costs had risen, particularly for utilities and pitch maintenance. After discussion, it was agreed that a modest increase was necessary but that the committee should be mindful of the impact on families. It was proposed and seconded that the fees for the next season be set at £48 for a full adult member, £27 for a junior, £16 for a social member, and £105 for a family. The proposal was carried unanimously.

**Decision 8.2:** Membership fees for the 2023/24 season to be set at: full adult £48; junior £27; social member £16; family £105. The increase to be communicated to members with the renewal notices in June.

**Action 8.4:** P. Delaney to update the membership fee schedule and inform the club website administrator. Deadline: 15 April.

The committee then considered a proposal from the Chair to introduce a reduced rate for full-time students and those on means-tested benefits. The Chair noted that the club had a stated aim of widening access to the sport and that a concessionary rate would support this. L. Bennett supported the idea but advised that the club would need a simple and consistent way of verifying eligibility. After discussion, it was agreed that a concessionary rate of £30 per season would be introduced, with proof of eligibility required at the point of joining or renewal. The committee noted that this would be reviewed after one year.

**Decision 8.3:** A concessionary membership rate of £30 per season to be introduced for full-time students and those in receipt of means-tested benefits, subject to proof of eligibility. To be reviewed at the AGM in 2024.

**Action 8.5:** L. Bennett to draft a short eligibility policy and a list of acceptable proofs for the concessionary rate. Deadline: 21 April.

Finally, the committee briefly discussed the club's membership data and data protection. K. Brooks reminded the committee that the club holds personal data on members and that the privacy notice on the website should be reviewed. The committee agreed that this would be added to the agenda for the next meeting.

**Action 8.6:** M. Fernandes to add a review of the club's privacy notice to the agenda for the May meeting.

The committee minutes record that Lucy Bennett was appointed as membership officer on 2023-04-01. Record status: current.

A. Cole reported that the winter programme of pitch maintenance had been completed, with the final dressing and seeding of the main pitch carried out in the last week of March. He noted that the new drainage channel along the western edge of the pitch had performed well during the recent wet spell. The committee thanked A. Cole and the grounds volunteers for their work.

A. Cole also reported that the clubhouse boiler had been serviced and that a minor leak in the gents' cloakroom had been repaired. He raised the question of the clubhouse external paintwork, which had not been done for several years and was beginning to look shabby. The committee agreed that this was a matter for the next budget cycle and asked A. Cole to obtain two or three quotes for the work.

**Action 9.1:** A. Cole to obtain quotes for repainting the clubhouse exterior and report back to the committee. Deadline: 30 April.

The committee noted that T. Okafor had taken up his post as Facilities Manager that morning and that he had already been in touch with A. Cole regarding the maintenance log. A. Cole confirmed that he had handed over the keys and the log as agreed.

**Committee Meeting Minutes – 6 May 2023**

**Present:** M. Fernandes (Chair), S. Granger (Vice-Chair), P. Delaney (Treasurer), A. Cole (Grounds), T. Okafor (Facilities Manager), D. Clarke (Head Coach), R. Singh (Membership Secretary), L. Whitfield (Social Secretary)

**Apologies:** J. Barlow (Youth Development), C. Hargreaves (Welfare Officer)

**Minutes of the previous meeting:** The minutes of the meeting held on 1 April 2023 were approved as a true record. Matters arising were noted as follows:

- Action 9.1 (quotes for repainting clubhouse exterior): A. Cole reported that he had obtained three quotes, ranging from £4,800 to £6,200. The committee agreed to defer the decision pending the budget review at the May meeting.
- Action 10.1 (AGM notice): M. Fernandes confirmed that the notice had been circulated to members by email and posted on the club noticeboard on 18 May. No errors had been reported.

---

**1. Chair's Welcome**

The Chair welcomed D. Clarke to his first committee meeting in his new role and thanked him for attending at short notice.

---

**2. Appointment of Head Coach**

The Chair reported that the selection panel had concluded its process and that a single candidate had been recommended for appointment. The committee had previously delegated authority to the panel to make the appointment, subject to satisfactory references and a satisfactory medical questionnaire.

The committee minutes record that Daniel Clarke was appointed as head coach on 2023-05-01. Record status: current. The appointment is current and takes effect from 1 May 2023, with a review scheduled after the first six months.

The Chair noted that D. Clarke had been released from his previous club without a transfer fee and that his coaching qualifications (UEFA B Licence) had been verified. The committee formally ratified the appointment and welcomed D. Clarke to the club.

**Action 1.1:** P. Delaney to update the club's insurance policy to include D. Clarke as a named coach. Deadline: 15 May.

---

**3. Head Coach's Report – D. Clarke**

D. Clarke presented his initial report on the playing side.

He had met with the senior squad on 2 May and had been impressed by the attitude of the players. He had also met with the youth section coaches and planned to observe training sessions over the next two weeks.

D. Clarke proposed the following changes to the training schedule:

- Senior squad training to move from Tuesday/Thursday to Tuesday/Thursday/Friday (Friday sessions to be optional, recovery-based).
- A pre-season fitness programme to begin on 1 July, with a testing day on 5 July.
- Goalkeeper-specific sessions to be introduced on Wednesday evenings, to be run by an external coach (to be confirmed).

The committee discussed the proposed changes. S. Granger raised a concern about the availability of the floodlights on Friday evenings, as the current booking ran to 9.30pm. T. Okafor confirmed that the floodlight booking could be extended to 10.00pm at no additional cost, subject to a revised booking with the council. The committee agreed to the revised schedule.

**Decision 3.1:** The committee approved the revised senior training schedule (Tuesday, Thursday, and optional Friday) with effect from 1 June 2023.

**Decision 3.2:** The committee approved the pre-season fitness programme as proposed, with the testing day on 5 July.

**Action 3.1:** D. Clarke to confirm the availability of the external goalkeeping coach and report back. Deadline: 20 May.

**Action 3.2:** T. Okafor to update the floodlight booking with the council to reflect the extended Friday hours. Deadline: 15 May.

---

**4. Player Development and Youth Section**

D. Clarke reported that he had reviewed the club's player development pathway and had identified a gap between the under-16 and under-18 age groups. He proposed that the club enter an under-18 team in the local league for the coming season, subject to the availability of players and a coach.

The committee noted that the youth section currently had 42 registered players across the under-8 to under-16 age groups. R. Singh confirmed that the membership database had been updated and that no duplicate records had been found.

environmental health officer on 28 March and had passed the inspection with no issues raised.

renewal was expected to proceed on the same terms. He noted that the council had asked whether
the club would be interested in taking on the maintenance of the adjacent car park, which was
currently maintained by the council. The committee discussed this briefly and agreed to defer a
decision until the next meeting, when the costs could be considered.

**Action 6.1:** T. Okafor to obtain a quote for the maintenance of the car park and report back.
Deadline: 1 June.

The Chair asked whether there were any other facility matters to discuss. R. Singh noted that the
club's defibrillator had been checked and was in working order. She also noted that the first-aid

documents.title: Committee Meeting Minutes – 1 April 2023
documents.content:
**8. Financial Review**

The Treasurer, P. Whitfield, presented the income and expenditure figures for the period
1 January to 30 April 2023. He circulated a summary sheet and noted that the club's
current account balance stood at £4,312.66 as of the close of business on 28 April.
This compared with a balance of £3,845.20 at the end of March.

Income for the four-month period was reported as follows:

- Membership fees: £6,240.00 (178 full members at £30.00 and 42 youth members at £15.00,
  with a small number of pro-rata payments for new joiners)
- Match fees and training fees: £1,865.50
- Clubhouse bar and tea bar takings: £1,120.75
- Sponsorship from the local garage, received in February: £500.00
- Donations collected at the community event in March: £184.60

Total income: £9,910.85.

Expenditure for the same period:

- Pitch maintenance and grounds (including grass cutting and line marking): £1,240.00
- Utility bills for the clubhouse (electricity and water): £986.40
- Insurance premium (annual, paid in January): £1,150.00
- Kitchen restocking and cleaning supplies: £312.20
- First-aid kit restocking: £87.50
- Defibrillator service: £45.00
- Affiliation fees to the county association: £320.00
- Printing and postage for the newsletter: £178.90
- Miscellaneous (including tea, coffee, and biscuits for the tea bar): £214.60

Total expenditure: £4,534.60.

The Treasurer noted that the net surplus for the period was £5,376.25. He reminded the
committee that the figure included the one-off insurance premium and that the next
quarter's figures would not include this cost. He also flagged that the club's annual
audit was due to be completed by the end of June and that he would need to gather
receipts and bank statements from the other signatories on the account.

The Chair asked whether the club had any outstanding debts or invoices. The Treasurer
confirmed that there were two outstanding invoices: one from the grounds contractor for
£180.00, which was due to be paid by 15 May, and one from the county association for
the affiliation fee, which had already been settled. He noted that the grounds
contractor's invoice had been received late and that he would chase it up if necessary.

**Decision 8.1:** The committee agreed to set aside a contingency fund of £1,000.00
from the current balance to cover any unexpected maintenance costs over the summer.
This would be held in the current account but recorded separately in the accounts.
The Treasurer was asked to note this in the club's financial records.

**Action 8.1:** P. Whitfield to chase the grounds contractor's invoice and arrange
payment by 15 May. Deadline: 15 May.

**Action 8.2:** P. Whitfield to circulate the full income and expenditure summary to
all committee members by email. Deadline: 8 May.

**Action 8.3:** P. Whitfield to prepare the paperwork for the annual audit and liaise
with the independent examiner. Deadline: 15 June.

The committee thanked the Treasurer for his report.

**9. Any Other Business**

The Chair invited any further items for discussion.

R. Singh raised the matter of the club's social media presence. She noted that the
club's Facebook page had not been updated since February and that a number of
prospective members had asked about training times via the page. She offered to take
on the role of updating the page on a weekly basis, posting fixtures, results, and
training information. The committee agreed that this would be a good use of her time
and thanked her for volunteering.

**Action 9.1:** R. Singh to update the club's Facebook page at least once a week,
starting immediately. No deadline.

T. Okafor mentioned that the council had contacted him again regarding the car park
maintenance question. He confirmed that the council had no immediate deadline for a
decision but had asked for an indication of interest by the end of May. The committee
reiterated that a decision would be made at the next meeting, as minuted earlier.

The Chair noted that the club's annual general meeting was scheduled for 12 June at
7.30pm in the clubhouse. He reminded the committee that nominations for the committee
positions would need to be received by the Secretary at least 14 days before the AGM,
in accordance with the club's constitution. He asked the Secretary to circulate a
reminder to all members with the agenda and the nomination form.

documents.content:
**10. Date of Next Meeting**

The next meeting of the committee will be held on Monday 1 May 2023 at 7.30pm in the clubhouse. The Secretary will circulate the agenda and any papers by email no later than Thursday 27 April.

**11. Correspondence and Reports**

The Secretary reported the following items of correspondence received since the last meeting:

- A letter from the local parish council confirming that the club's application for a grant towards the cost of new sight screens had been successful. The grant of £1,250 would be paid into the club's bank account within 28 days. The Chair asked the Treasurer to acknowledge receipt of the grant in writing and to ensure that the funds were allocated to the sight screen fund in the accounts.
- An email from the league secretary confirming the fixture list for the coming season. The fixture list had been circulated to all team captains by email on 28 March. Any queries regarding fixtures should be raised with the Fixtures Secretary, T. Okafor, before the start of the season.
- A letter from a local resident complaining about noise from the clubhouse on the evening of Saturday 25 March. The resident, Mrs D. Hartley of 14 Meadow Lane, stated that music could be heard from her property until after 11.30pm. The committee discussed the matter and agreed that a polite reply should be sent apologising for any disturbance and confirming that the club would remind all hirers of the clubhouse of the noise restrictions contained in their hire agreements. The Chair asked the Secretary to draft the reply and to log the complaint in the club's correspondence file.

The Chair reported that he had attended a meeting of the local sports forum on 22 March on behalf of the club. The forum had discussed the proposed development of a new all-weather pitch at the recreation ground. No firm decision had been taken, but the forum had agreed to circulate a survey to local sports clubs to gauge demand. The Chair would forward the survey to the committee when it arrived.

**12. Clubhouse and Facilities Report**

The Facilities Officer, M. Brennan, reported that the clubhouse had been cleaned and the windows replaced in accordance with the programme agreed at the previous meeting. He noted that the contractor had completed the work on time and within budget. The committee thanked M. Brennan for his work.

M. Brennan also reported that the boiler had been serviced on 27 March. The service had revealed no faults, and the engineer had confirmed that the boiler was in good working order for the coming months. The service record had been filed in the clubhouse office.

The committee noted that the external lights at the rear of the clubhouse were not working. M. Brennan had tested the lights and believed that the issue was with the timer switch. He agreed to replace the switch and to report back at the next meeting.

**13. Membership Report**

The Membership Secretary, R. Singh, reported that the club currently had 214 full members and 38 junior members. She noted that this was a slight increase on the same time last year, and that the club had received a number of enquiries following the open day held in March. She had sent membership packs to all new members and had updated the membership database.

R. Singh also reported that the club had received a number of requests for information about the junior coaching programme. She had forwarded these to the Junior Coordinator, who would be in touch with the families concerned. The committee agreed that the junior section was in a healthy position and thanked R. Singh for her work.

**14. Team Reports**

The First XI Captain, T. Okafor, reported that pre-season training had begun on Tuesday 28 March and was being held on Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 6.30pm to 8.00pm. He confirmed that the club had a full fixture list for the coming season and that all players had been notified of the start of training. He noted that two players had indicated that they would be unavailable for the first few matches of the season due to work commitments, but that he expected to have a full squad available for the first league match on 22 April.
